items.text: Explain what S3 is and how it differs from EBS and EFS
Describe what a bucket is and why bucket names must be globally unique
Explain what an object is, what a key is, and how an S3 URL is structured
State the maximum object size (5 TB) and the maximum single PUT upload size (5 GB)
Explain when and why Multipart Upload is used
List all S3 storage classes and describe the use case for each
Explain what 11 nines of durability means and how S3 achieves it
Describe how S3 Versioning works and the two things it protects against
Created an S3 bucket with a unique name in a specific region
Uploaded an object and inspected its properties and URL
Changed the storage class of an uploaded object
Enabled versioning on a bucket and uploaded multiple versions of the same file
Used Show Versions to view all object versions with their Version IDs
Simulated accidental deletion and restored the object by removing the delete marker
Distinguish between the 5 TB object size limit and the 5 GB single PUT limit
Identify which storage classes have no retrieval fee (Standard and Intelligent-Tiering)
Identify which storage class stores data in a single AZ (One Zone-IA)
Recall minimum storage durations: IA = 30 days, Glacier Instant/Flexible = 90 days, Deep Archive = 180 days
Explain the difference between Compliance mode and Governance mode in Object Lock
Describe what a delete marker is and how to restore an object by removing it
